sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ready to learn **Programming Style and Documentation**?

Here's what we'll cover:

• Best practices for writing clean and documented code
• Why this matters for your coding journey
• Hands-on examples you can try

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Think of **Programming Style and Documentation** like building blocks. 

Every great program starts with small, simple pieces. This is one of those essential pieces!

• Start simple, then build up
• Practice makes it click
• Don't worry if it takes time - totally normal!

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Use meaningful variable and method names that describe their purpose
Indent code blocks consistently to improve readability
Write comments to explain the purpose of code, not what it does literally
Javadoc comments (/** */) generate API documentation from source code
Follow established conventions: classes in PascalCase, variables in camelCase

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Programming Style and Documentation - Best practices for writing clean and documented code. Master basics before advancing. Practice with the examples. Builds foundation for what's next.

questions.question: Which of the following is a proper single-line comment in Java?
questions.explanation: In Java, single-line comments start with //. Everything after // on that line is ignored by the compiler. Multi-line comments use /* */.

questions.question: What is the recommended naming convention for variables in Java?
questions.explanation: Java convention uses camelCase for variable and method names (e.g., myVariable, calculateArea). Class names use PascalCase, and constants use ALL_CAPS.
